E1.evidence: Reproducer "RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_cyclonedds_cpp  gazebo -s libgazebo_ros_init.so /usr/share/gazebo-11/worlds/elevator.world" with log line "1652881428.257805 []   gzserver: create_thread: gzserver: no free slot"; the Cyclone DDS maintainer points to cyclonedds#479 and the reporter confirms "The problem is fixed by building a custom build of cyclonedds." -- https://github.com/ros2/rmw_cyclonedds/issues/395

E2.evidence: The crash is caused by a fixed-size thread-state table inside the Cyclone DDS library, which runs out of slots when enough threads use it on a many-core machine; no value, name, frame, unit, or timing crosses a boundary, and any correct application using that many threads triggers it. The reporter's fix changes only the library's own constant: "As for a 128 cores machine, the max number of threads is changed from \"64\" to \"256\"  (Tested \"128\" but still failed) in the source file: [cyclonedds/src/core/ddsc/src/dds_init.c] ... thread_states_init (64);" -- https://github.com/ros2/rmw_cyclonedds/issues/395. The linked upstream issue describes the same limit: "Probably cause could be caused by the fixed number of max. allocated threads here" and the maintainer: "Once again proof that every quick workaround comes back to bite one ... I'd prefer a change that removes the limit altogether" -- https://github.com/eclipse-cyclonedds/cyclonedds/issues/479. A resource limit inside one library is ineligible `internal`.

E3.evidence: Not evaluated past E2. The failure appears while gzserver runs with Cyclone DDS (both active in one process).

E4.evidence: "Gzserver crashes within several minutes after starting with the following logging." -- https://github.com/ros2/rmw_cyclonedds/issues/395

ineligible_reason: internal: Cyclone DDS's hard-coded thread-state table (thread_states_init(64)) is exhausted on a 128-core machine; a capacity limit inside one library that any correct many-threaded application triggers.
notes: Setup reported: Ubuntu 20.04, ROS 2 Foxy binaries, rmw_cyclonedds 0.7.3, Gazebo 11 in Docker on a 128-core host; the working custom build used cyclonedds branch release/0.7.x and rmw_cyclonedds branch foxy with the constant raised to 256. Upstream cyclonedds later removed the limit (per cyclonedds#479: "This was solved, once and for all, by https://github.com/eclipse-cyclonedds/cyclonedds/pull/1290"). The packet's fix commits are in a downstream project (Nova-UTD/navigator), not by the rmw_cyclonedds or cyclonedds maintainers: c316a7e8 (2022-10-31) has the message "Fix CycloneDDS error - https://github.com/ros2/rmw_cyclonedds/issues/395 - Removed CycloneDDS apt package, build from source under /src/external"; its Dockerfile diff replaces `apt install -y ros-foxy-rmw-cyclonedds-cpp` with a sysctl receive-buffer setting. 05f55430, 1d40ba01 and 659ccb0a are large squash commits (all titled "v1.3.1 - Add MCL, mapping tools, and leaderboard connection improvments (#304)", committer date 2023-01-21) whose messages include the same bullet. These are build/packaging workarounds in a third project and would themselves be `build`. Reason code judgment: the limit is not a declared interface attribute of either unit; it could alternatively be argued to be an undocumented capacity assumption between application and library, which none of the listed failure classes covers.
